intro: Lesson 6: How can we explain the First Crusade?. To understand the causes of the First Crusade and the motives of those who joined

questions.q: Write a PEEL point about religious motives.
questions.a: Point: many crusaders were driven by religion. Evidence: the Pope promised forgiveness of sins. Explain: so they believed going would save their souls. Link: so religion was a key cause.
questions.model: Point: Many crusaders went for religious reasons. Evidence: Urban II promised forgiveness of sins. Explain: they believed this would save them from punishment after death. Link: so religion explains why so many joined.

questions.a: For example: land, riches or fame

questions.q: Why did the Byzantine emperor want help?
questions.a: To win back land lost to the Seljuks

questions.q: Core: Write a PEEL paragraph in the portal response box: 'The most important reason people joined the First Crusade was ...'
questions.a: A clear point, evidence (forgiveness, land, adventure), explanation and link back to the question
questions.model: Teacher goes through it first: 'The most important reason was religion (P). The Pope promised forgiveness of sins (E). For people who feared punishment in the hereafter, this was powerful (E). So religion explains why even the poor joined (L).'

questions.q: Extend: Add a sentence on a second motive and why it is less important.
questions.a: For example: Some wanted land, but most knights spent their own money and many returned home poorer

questions.q: Stretch: Was the Pope's motive the same as the crusaders'? Explain.
questions.a: Partly: he wanted to help Byzantium and strengthen his own power, while many crusaders sought forgiveness or land

questions.q: The Pope called the crusade at:
Big question: why would thousands of people walk 3,000 km to fight?
questions.a: Religious belief (forgiveness, pilgrimage), hope of land and riches, adventure and status, and the Pope's call
